evidence_snippets: Example This example performs a scoped COUNT aggregation and then filters and sorts the records by the aggregated value. legacySQL SELECT repository . url , COUNT ( payload . pages . page name ) WITHIN RECORD AS page count FROM [ bigquery - public - data : samples . github nested ] HAVING page count > 80 ORDER BY page count DESC ; FROM clause FROM [project name:]datasetId.tableId [ [ AS ] alias ] ( subquery ) [ [ AS ] alias ] JOIN clause FLATTEN clause table wildcard function The FROM clause specifies the source data to be queried.

If you use OMIT...IF to exclude a portion of a record in a repeating field, and the query also selects other independently repeating fields, BigQuery omits a portion of the other repeated records in the query.
Given a record with one or more values for a repeated field, FLATTEN will create multiple records, one for each value in the repeated field.
